title: 面试被问讲一次工作失误和补救经过
titleEn: Answering "Tell me about a time you made a mistake"
scene: 周三下午，你在一家市政厅（Riverside Council，虚构）参加业务分析师（BA）岗位的面对面面试。面试官是数字服务组的经理 Andrew，说话快、爱开玩笑。前面聊得不错，他突然说：“Righto, here's a bit of a curly one — tell me about a time you dropped the ball at work.” 很多人一听“犯错”就紧张，要么说“我想不出来”，要么把错推给别人——这两种都会扣分。澳洲面试官想看的是：你敢不敢承认（own up to it）、怎么补救、学到了什么。
你的目标：① 用 STAR（情境–任务–行动–结果）讲清一次真实但不致命的失误：上一份工作中需求遗漏了兼职员工的假期计算，UAT 时才发现；② 听懂 Andrew 的快语速追问（in hindsight、slip through the cracks、throw someone under the bus），不确定时礼貌澄清；③ 最后讲出你改了什么流程，让失误变成加分项。

facts.v: 周三下午 2:00，面对面面试，约 45 分钟
需求漏了兼职员工假期按比例计算 → UAT 发现 → 当天上报、三天修好、上线只推迟两天
加了一张“边界情况检查清单”，每次需求评审都过一遍

vocab.ex: Tell me about a time you dropped the ball at work.
I owned up to it straight away and told my manager.
How did that slip through the cracks?

vocab.zh: 把责任推给别人、出卖别人
vocab.ex: I didn't want to throw the developer under the bus.

vocab.en: a curly one / a curly question
vocab.ex: Here's a bit of a curly one for you.
We found the issue two weeks before go-live.
Part-time staff were an edge case we missed.
In hindsight, I should have checked with payroll earlier.
I took that feedback on board.

vocab.zh: 坦然接受批评/后果（澳洲口语）
vocab.ex: I just copped it on the chin and focused on the fix.
Leave for part-timers is calculated pro rata.
Fair enough — no-one gets it right every time.

listening.en: Righto, here's a bit of a curly one — tell me about a time you dropped the ball.
listening.sound: Righto 读 “rai-toh”（好嘞）；bit of a 连读成 “bidda”；a curly one = 刁钻的问题；dropped the ball 中 dropped 的 -ed 几乎听不到，像 “drop-the-ball”。
listening.zh: 好，来个有点刁钻的——讲讲你在工作中搞砸过的一次。
listening.reply: Sure. There's one that comes to mind from my last role.

listening.en: So how'd that slip through the cracks in the first place?
listening.sound: how'd = how did，读 “howd”；slip through the 连成 “slip-throo-the”；in the first place 读快像 “in-the-fus-place”，意思是“最初、到底”。
listening.zh: 那一开始这事是怎么被漏掉的？
listening.reply: Honestly, I assumed the leave rules were the same for everyone, and I didn't double-check with payroll.

listening.en: And you didn't wanna throw the devs under the bus, I s'pose?
listening.sound: wanna = want to；devs = developers（开发人员）；I s'pose = I suppose，读 “I spose”，放在句尾表示“我猜”。throw…under the bus = 甩锅给别人。
listening.zh: 而且我猜你也不想把锅甩给开发吧？
listening.reply: No, not at all. The requirement came from me, so it was my call to own it.

listening.en: Did your boss go off at you, or was she pretty good about it?
listening.sound: go off at someone 是澳洲口语，“冲某人发火”；was she 连成 “wo-zshe”；pretty good about it = 处理得挺通情达理。
listening.zh: 你老板有没有冲你发火，还是她挺通情达理的？
listening.reply: She was pretty good about it, actually. She appreciated that I came to her straight away with a plan.

listening.en: In hindsight, what would you do differently, d'you reckon?
listening.sound: d'you reckon 读 “jer-reckon”，意思是“你觉得呢”，澳洲人常放在问句末尾；in hindsight = 事后回想。
listening.zh: 事后回想，你觉得自己会怎么做得不一样？
listening.reply: I'd bring in the people who actually use the system much earlier, and go through the edge cases with them.

listening.en: Good stuff. Fair enough — no-one's perfect. Let's crack on.
listening.sound: Good stuff = 很好；no-one's 读 “no-wunz”；crack on = 继续往下进行（英澳口语）。听到这句说明这一题过了。
listening.zh: 很好。可以理解——没人是完美的。我们继续吧。

speech.topic: 我从一次工作失误中学到的事
paragraphs: I'd like to talk about a mistake I made at work, and what I learnt from it. A couple of years ago, I was working as a business analyst on a new leave system for about eight hundred staff. My job was to collect the requirements and make sure the system did what people needed.

Two weeks before go-live, we were doing user testing, and a tester found a problem. Leave for part-time staff wasn't being calculated pro rata. Some people would have got too much leave, and some too little. When I checked my documents, I realised it was my mistake. I had assumed the rules were the same for everyone, and I hadn't double-checked with payroll.

My first feeling was panic. But I knew hiding it would only make it worse. So I owned up to it that same morning. I went to my manager, explained what had happened, and showed her a plan to fix it. I didn't blame the developers, because the requirement came from me.

Then I worked closely with payroll and the developers. We fixed the rule in three days and tested it again with real examples. In the end, go-live was only two days late, and nobody's pay was affected.

The biggest lesson for me was about edge cases. Now I keep a simple checklist: part-time staff, casuals, people on leave, and anyone who starts or finishes in the middle of a month. I go through it in every requirements meeting. I also learnt that people respect you more when you're honest early. A mistake is not the end of the world if you deal with it quickly and learn from it.
speech.zh: 我想讲一次工作中的失误和我学到的东西。几年前我做 BA，负责一个约 800 名员工使用的新休假系统，负责收集需求。上线前两周的用户测试中，测试人员发现兼职员工的假期没有按比例计算。我一查发现是我的错：我以为所有人规则一样，没和薪资部门核实。我先是慌了，但知道隐瞒只会更糟，于是当天上午就向经理承认，说明经过并给出补救方案，没有把责任推给开发。之后我和薪资部门、开发紧密合作，三天修好并用真实案例重测，上线只推迟两天，没有影响任何人的工资。最大的收获是重视边界情况：现在我有一张检查清单（兼职、临时工、休假中的人、月中入职或离职的人），每次需求会都过一遍。我也明白了，早点坦白反而更让人尊重；只要尽快处理并从中学习，犯错不是世界末日。

patterns.en: When I checked ___, I realised it was my mistake.
patterns.zh: 当我查看___时，我意识到是我的错。（my documents / the email / the numbers）

patterns.en: I owned up to it ___ and showed my manager ___.
patterns.zh: 我___就承认了，并给经理看了___。（that same morning / a plan to fix it）
最后，___，而且___。用来讲 STAR 的 Result。

patterns.en: The biggest lesson for me was ___. Now I ___.
patterns.zh: 对我最大的教训是___。现在我会___。用来收尾，讲改进。

other.name: Andrew
other.role: 数字服务组经理（面试官）

lines.en: Okay, that's great, thanks. Righto, here's a bit of a curly one for you. Tell me about a time you dropped the ball at work.
lines.zh: 好，很好，谢谢。来，问个有点刁钻的。讲讲你在工作中搞砸过的一次。

lines.en: Sure. Sorry, just to confirm — you mean a time I made a mistake, and how I handled it?
lines.zh: 好的。不好意思，确认一下——您是说我犯过的一次错，以及我是怎么处理的？

lines.en: Yep, spot on. Doesn't have to be a disaster. I'm more interested in what you did about it.
lines.zh: 对，没错。不一定是什么大灾难，我更关心你后来怎么做的。

lines.en: Okay. In my last role, I was the BA on a new leave system for about eight hundred staff. I was responsible for gathering all the requirements.
lines.zh: 好。在上一份工作里，我是一个新休假系统的 BA，大约八百名员工使用。我负责收集所有需求。

lines.en: Right, so a fair bit riding on it, then.
lines.zh: 嗯，那这事挺要紧的。

lines.en: Yes, definitely. About two weeks before go-live, during user testing, a tester noticed that leave for part-time staff wasn't being calculated pro rata.
lines.zh: 是的。上线前大约两周，在用户测试时，一名测试人员发现兼职员工的假期没有按比例计算。

lines.en: Ah, yep. Classic. So how'd that slip through the cracks in the first place?
lines.zh: 啊，对，典型问题。那一开始这事是怎么被漏掉的？

lines.en: Sorry, could you say that again a bit slower?
lines.zh: 不好意思，您能说慢一点再说一遍吗？

lines.en: Course. How did the problem get missed? How did nobody pick it up earlier?
lines.zh: 当然。这个问题是怎么被漏掉的？怎么之前没人发现？

lines.en: Honestly, that part was on me. I assumed the leave rules were the same for everyone, and I didn't double-check with payroll. So the requirement I wrote was incomplete.
lines.zh: 老实说，那是我的责任。我以为所有人的假期规则都一样，没有和薪资部门核实，所以我写的需求不完整。

lines.en: Okay, fair enough. And you didn't wanna throw the devs under the bus, I s'pose?
lines.zh: 好，可以理解。我猜你也不想把锅甩给开发吧？

lines.en: No, not at all. The developers built exactly what I wrote. So that same morning, I went to my manager and owned up to it.
lines.zh: 完全不会。开发完全按我写的做了。所以当天上午我就去找经理，主动承认了。

lines.en: Good on ya. Did she go off at you, or was she pretty good about it?
lines.zh: 好样的。她有没有冲你发火，还是挺通情达理的？

lines.en: Just to check — 'go off at me' means 'get angry with me'?
lines.zh: 确认一下——“go off at me”是“对我发火”的意思吗？

lines.en: Yeah, yeah, sorry — Aussie-ism. Did she lose it?
lines.zh: 对对，不好意思，澳洲说法。她有没有发脾气？

lines.en: No, she was pretty good about it. I think it helped that I didn't just bring the problem — I brought a plan. I'd already talked to payroll and the lead developer about a fix.
lines.zh: 没有，她挺通情达理的。我想是因为我不只是带着问题去，还带了方案。我已经和薪资部门、开发组长谈过怎么修。

lines.en: Right. And how'd it pan out in the end? Did go-live get pushed back?
lines.zh: 嗯。那最后结果怎么样？上线推迟了吗？

lines.en: Only by two days. We fixed the rule in three days and retested it with real examples from payroll — casuals, part-timers, people starting mid-month. Nobody's pay was affected.
lines.zh: 只推迟了两天。我们三天修好了规则，并用薪资部门提供的真实案例重测——临时工、兼职、月中入职的人。没有任何人的工资受影响。

lines.en: Oh, that's not bad at all. And how'd the payroll team take it? They can be a bit of a tough crowd, in my experience.
lines.zh: 哦，那还不错。薪资部门那边反应怎么样？据我经验，他们可不太好打交道。

lines.en: They were actually really helpful. I think they appreciated being asked. Since then, I've made a point of checking in with them early on every project.
lines.zh: 他们其实非常帮忙。我觉得他们挺高兴被请教的。从那以后，每个项目我都会尽早找他们确认。

lines.en: Nice. In hindsight, what would you do differently, d'you reckon?
lines.zh: 不错。事后回想，你觉得自己会怎么做得不一样？

lines.en: I'd bring the actual users in much earlier. Now I keep an edge-case checklist — part-time, casual, people on leave, mid-month starters — and I go through it in every requirements workshop.
lines.zh: 我会更早把真正的使用者拉进来。现在我有一张边界情况检查清单——兼职、临时工、休假中的人、月中入职的人——每次需求研讨会都过一遍。

lines.en: Love that. Honestly, a lot of people just say they can't think of anything, which is a bit of a red flag for us. Good stuff — let's crack on.
lines.zh: 很好。说实话，很多人就说想不出来，这对我们来说有点危险信号。很好——我们继续吧。

lines.en: Thanks, Andrew. It wasn't fun at the time, but I learnt a lot from it.
lines.zh: 谢谢 Andrew。当时挺不好受的，但我从中学到了很多。

rescue.en: Sorry, could you say that again a bit slower?
rescue.zh: 不好意思，能说慢一点再说一遍吗？

rescue.en: Just to confirm, you're asking about ___?
Sorry, I'm not familiar with that expression — what does it mean?
rescue.zh: 不好意思，我不太熟悉这个说法，是什么意思？

rescue.en: That's a good question. Can I have a moment to think of the best example?
rescue.zh: 好问题。能给我一点时间想个最合适的例子吗？

rescue.en: Would you mind sending the next steps by email, just so I have them in writing?
rescue.zh: 能麻烦您把后续步骤发邮件给我吗？这样我有书面记录。

checklist: 我能用 STAR 结构讲一次真实但不致命的工作失误，不超过两分钟
我没有说“想不出来”，也没有把责任推给别人（throw someone under the bus）
我听懂了 drop the ball、slip through the cracks、go off at someone、in hindsight
被问“你会怎么做得不一样”时，我能说出一个具体的改进（如检查清单）
听不懂俚语时，我能用 “Just to check — ___ means ___?” 礼貌确认
我能用 owned up to it、took it on board、in the end 这类表达讲结果和收获
